Package dev.opencollab.paletter

Class PaletteLayer

java.lang.Object
dev.opencollab.paletter.PaletteLayer
public final class PaletteLayer extends Object
A patch on top of a palette: custom items and blocks, changes to vanilla items, creative inventory edits, tags. Content only, fallbacks and creative ordering are policy of the Paletter. Layers are immutable and independent of protocol versions; the same layer is compiled against every version.

Palettes are built by stacking layers, so ownership can be split. For example:

  1. a geyser layer with Geyser's own fixes and custom items, compiled once per version and shared;
  2. an extensions layer with custom items and blocks of extensions, also shared;
  3. a per-session layer, e.g. content of the server the player is on, applied with Palette.extend(dev.opencollab.paletter.PaletteLayer).
A later layer sees everything earlier layers did. Definitions untouched by a layer are shared with the palette it extends, so the per-session palette costs little and its definitions stay == to the shared ones. Canonical ids never change: custom content is appended. Block runtime ids are state hashes, so adding custom blocks does not change the ids of other blocks.

Thread safety: a built layer is immutable and may be shared between threads and compiled by several palettes at once. Its PaletteLayer.Builder is not thread safe. The callbacks given to the builder (PaletteLayer.Builder.creative(Consumer), PaletteLayer.Builder.overrideItem(String, Consumer)) are called while a palette is compiled, once per compilation and data version, possibly from any thread; they must not depend on external mutable state.

Null handling: everything is @NonNull unless marked; the builder methods throw NullPointerException for null. Problems with the content (a duplicate identifier, a hash collision) are not found here but when a palette compiles the layer: Paletter.Builder.build() and Palette.extend(dev.opencollab.paletter.PaletteLayer) throw a PaletteException. Content is named by keys, custom items and blocks create their own (see CustomItem, CustomBlock).

Since:
1.0.0
